title: Issue 2 Cover
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Issue 2 through the Jax/Astra/Brick triangle, not through break-room policy as an abstract problem. Jax wants to eat and instinctively routes around nonsense; Astra cannot stop trying to make a shared space workable; Brick treats even a microwave dispute with the gravity of a security incident. The break-room bureaucracy is the catalyst that lets three personalities collide.
settingText: Stardust Station shared break room at lunch: maintained microwave, shared refrigerator, vending unit, mismatched chairs, ordinary food containers and an excessive but visually secondary layer of blank notices/forms. Bright, familiar StarTrust workplace; the room feels used by coworkers, not staged as a bureaucracy exhibit.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER. Jax owns the middle foreground at the microwave with an ordinary lunch container, relaxed but visibly unwilling to make lunch into a governance project. Astra is close enough to be in his space, holding or removing one fresh blank rule sheet while trying to mediate rather than police. Brick looms at the other side studying the microwave/refrigerator situation with completely sincere investigative gravity.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. The cover must read as three incompatible but familiar coworker instincts occupying one tiny room: Jax evades needless complexity, Astra tries to make people coexist, Brick cannot help treating a trivial anomaly as worthy of scrutiny. They know each other; this is not strangers performing a gag.
PROBLEM AS CATALYST. Notices, forms and arrows may crowd the edges, but they are background pressure. The reader should notice the characters' attitudes before noticing the paperwork.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead first; Jax/Astra/Brick social triangle second; microwave/lunch third; procedural clutter last. Faces, posture and eye-lines are more important than any prop text.
THUMBNAIL READ. Three unmistakably different silhouettes arranged around one microwave: Jax casual, Astra managing, Brick intensely serious. The joke survives even if every notice becomes unreadable.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not depict the final break-room rules, a solved governance system, a triumphant meal, or any end-of-issue consensus. Promise the coworker collision, not its resolution.

title: Issue 3 Cover
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Issue 3 through the social choreography of ownership: Astra needs somebody to own three ordinary tasks, while Jax, Glorp and Zib each reveal a different personality in the act of not becoming the obvious volunteer. The tasks are intentionally boring; the entertainment is watching coworkers negotiate responsibility without saying that is what they are doing.
settingText: Small Stardust operations meeting table during a supposedly quick ownership discussion: three plain task folders, one pen, too many chairs, drinks and tablets, with normal station work visible beyond. The table is familiar shared territory, not a formal boardroom.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER. Stage a visual relay around the table: Astra extends the pen or one ownerless folder toward Jax; Jax is already redirecting it toward Glorp with easy social deflection; Glorp receives it with formal concern and a binder ready; Zib reaches past the entire exchange for a practical tool or work item, visibly more interested in doing work than discussing who owns it.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. Astra organizes. Jax sidesteps. Glorp wants the process to be defensible. Zib wants the meeting to stop becoming a meeting. Their body language should make the group history legible without a single speech balloon.

PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The three tasks are visually plain and unimpressive. Do not make the folders ominous, glowing or theatrically important. The comedy comes from how much social energy four competent people spend around something this dull.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; the circular handoff among Astra/Jax/Glorp/Zib; the pen/folder as the shared pivot; empty chairs and ordinary station work behind them.
THUMBNAIL READ. Four distinct bodies around one table with the pen/folder visibly traveling sideways instead of landing. The cover should read as coworker chemistry before it reads as administration.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not reveal the eventual assignments, who finally accepts which task, or the meeting's resolution. No completed owner names.

title: Issue 4 Cover — Temporary Material
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Temporary Material through the Astra/Mira/Zib relationship: Astra worries about what institutions will do with a small finding, Mira insists on saying exactly what the evidence supports, and Zib refuses to let either of them turn an active repair into a seminar. The strange material and missing part are the excuse for this triangle, not the star.
settingText: Bright maintained Stardust maintenance bay with an open service panel, approved clamp/mesh hardware, a small non-glowing residue sample nearby and the unresolved bracket position visible. The bay is active working territory, not a discovery chamber.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER inspired by the issue's strongest social beat without reproducing a panel literally. Zib is half inside or crouched at the open service compartment and has physically made Astra and Mira useful: each is holding an opposite end of ordinary clamp/mesh hardware or a work light while they continue an intent, low-key argument across the repair.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. Astra and Mira are not enemies; they are protecting different risks and are annoyed by how close their positions actually are. Zib's expression/body language says the argument may continue as long as their hands keep helping. This three-way dynamic is the cover's real subject.

PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The residue sample stays small, ordinary and secondary. The missing bracket and temporary hardware explain why the three are together, but the reader's eye should stay on the personalities and eye-lines.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Astra/Mira face-to-face tension bridged physically by the repair hardware; Zib anchoring the practical work; open panel and tiny sample as context.
THUMBNAIL READ. Two coworkers locked in a serious disagreement while a third literally keeps them working. The repair reads as workplace context, not science-fiction spectacle.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the final successful temporary brace, completed report, commercial-interest flag or later corporate consequence. The hardware should still look provisional.

title: Issue 5 Cover — Resource Efficiency Review
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Resource Efficiency Review through Astra, Jax and Mira participating in the same corporate pilot for completely different reasons. Astra is willing to tolerate the program because the station needs a part; Jax turns vague corporate work into bounded physical responsibilities; Mira is genuinely interested in the material while refusing unsupported people-data claims. Their uneasy alliance is more interesting than the bins.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub during the limited pilot: one pristine corporate collection container has entered the lived-in station workspace among ordinary carts, tools, samples and work orders. The station remains active around it.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER. Astra stands with the pilot form/tablet, watching both coworkers rather than staring at corporate hardware. Jax is physically checking clearance or nudging the pristine collection container out of a real route with practical ease. Mira, on the opposite side, is absorbed in one legitimate sample with visible scientific curiosity. All three are participating, but none for the same reason.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. Astra needs the possibility of procurement help; Jax will support only work with clear edges; Mira will support only claims the material can actually bear. Their glances should suggest they know exactly what the others are doing and are choosing to work together anyway.

PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The corporate apparatus should be attractive, clean and reasonable, but visually subordinate to the three people negotiating around it. Do not make the cover 'Astra versus a bin.'
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; three-character triangle; Jax's route action and Mira's sample as opposing practical/scientific poles; corporate container and forms as context.

THUMBNAIL READ. Three strong personalities sharing one corporate object: manager evaluating, technician repositioning, scientist investigating. Their different relationships to the same program must survive at small size.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the crew's final boundary, exact accepted/refused terms, successful baseline, Wellness Week, or the later procurement result.

title: Issue 6 Cover — Wellness Week
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Wellness Week through the Zib/Astra/Noola triangle. Zib has a real ten-minute repair trapped behind a wellness setup, Noola simply refuses to remain physically uncomfortable, and Astra is the manager who tried to accommodate both the program and the station until those two realities became impossible to separate.
settingText: Multipurpose room mid-wellness session: soft chairs and tidy corporate setup in the foreground, a warm room and blocked wall service panel behind them, clear exit path to one side. Familiar Stardust workplace under temporary repurposing.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER. Noola is already rising from or moving away from one wellness chair with calm certainty—no melodrama, just 'this does not work for me.' Zib waits at the blocked service panel with his compact tool case, patient but visibly ready to fix the actual room. Astra stands between their trajectories with the session tablet/clipboard, realizing both coworkers are being more sensible than the program she is trying to manage.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. Noola's self-knowledge, Zib's practical patience and Astra's managerial responsibility must all read sympathetically. The humor comes from Astra being the only person still trying to make the incompatible arrangement hold together.
PROBLEM AS CATALYST. Chairs and wellness materials explain the collision but should not dominate the image. The people and their directional movement are the composition.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Noola exiting / Zib waiting / Astra caught between them; service panel and chairs as the spatial explanation.
THUMBNAIL READ. Three characters pull the composition in three directions: out the door, toward the panel, and stuck between. Their personalities should be legible before the wellness premise is.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the room being cleared, the repair completed, the quiet-room solution, collected data or the program's eventual outcome.

title: Issue 7 Cover — Bring Your Feelings to Work Day
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Bring Your Feelings to Work Day through the contrast between Kreeb/Noola's quiet trust and Brick's absolute seriousness about an absurd grievance. The issue works because genuine private feeling and ridiculous workplace complaint are allowed to coexist without the story mocking either the person or the need to be heard.
settingText: Stardust admin-hub / quiet-room threshold during the disclosure program: small participation table with blank cards and privacy envelopes near the quiet-room door; ordinary vending machine visible deeper in the working space.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER with two connected social beats in one depth composition. Foreground: Noola quietly offers Kreeb a sealed/folded card; Kreeb receives it without reaching for more information, calm and respectful. Background: Brick studies the vending machine with the posture of a detective who has finally found a worthy adversary.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. The foreground must feel genuinely safe and intimate without becoming sentimental. The background gag works because Brick is not joking. Kreeb's restraint is as character-defining as Brick's over-seriousness.
PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The disclosure box/cards are merely the device that puts these behaviors next to each other. Do not make the anonymous program the main visual subject.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Noola-to-Kreeb handoff and eye-line; Brick/vending-machine secondary story; participation materials last.
THUMBNAIL READ. A quiet two-person exchange in front, one unmistakably over-serious stone coworker investigating a vending machine behind them. Warmth and absurdity should coexist in a single glance.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not reveal Noola's disclosure text, the hatch fault, duplicate-process discovery, final reporting boundary or the corporate-visit consequence.

title: Issue 8 Cover — The Corporate Visit
summary: Character-first cover. Sell The Corporate Visit through Liaison/Astra/Jax chemistry: Astra wants the visit to go normally, Jax treats it as a route that must yield to real work, and the Liaison proves more interested in how the station actually functions than in being shown a polished presentation. Observation is pressure, but the people are the hook.
settingText: Docking vestibule opening onto the active Stardust working level. A planned visitor route immediately intersects ordinary carts, access lanes and service activity. Clean StarTrust threshold, lived-in station beyond.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER. The Operations Liaison has just stepped through the docking hatch with one compact case. Astra gives the smallest professional welcome while holding the planned route tablet. Jax, already several steps ahead, is physically redirecting the route around ordinary work—moving a barrier/cart or indicating an alternate path without waiting for the ceremonial part of the visit.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. Astra is managing impression, Jax is managing reality, and the Liaison's attention has already shifted toward Jax and the functioning station rather than toward Astra's presentation. No one is hostile; the subtle alliance forming between competence and honest observation is the intrigue.
PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The corporate visit is not a threat poster. The hatch, route and visitor badge explain why these three are together; their attitudes are what should sell the issue.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Liaison/Astra/Jax eye-line triangle; Jax's reroute gesture; active station beyond. Keep corporate symbols restrained.
THUMBNAIL READ. Visitor entering, manager welcoming, technician already rerouting them. The character dynamic should be obvious without interface text.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the galley fault, live repair, residue sample, visitor conclusion, pilot recommendation, central target or any outcome of the visit.

title: Issue 9 Cover — Output Target
summary: Character-first cover. Sell Output Target as an Astra/Mira/Jax character story about a competent manager beginning to bend herself toward a number because she wants something legitimate for the station. Mira sees the evidence problem; Jax sees the operational distortion; neither treats Astra as a villain. The metric matters because these coworkers know her well enough to notice what it is doing.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub at the maintenance-calendar worktable: current work and next-week task cards/slates coexist with a large clean abstract target display in the background. The station is still operating around the conversation.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED CHARACTER COVER. Astra sits or stands at the table with one hand hovering over a task that clearly belongs to later, her attention pulled toward the large target display behind. Mira is close on one side with sample/data material, watching Astra rather than the number. Jax stands on the other with today's route/work slate, also watching Astra. Their expressions are familiar concern, skepticism and recognition—not confrontation.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. Mira understands the scientific distortion; Jax understands the operational distortion; both understand why Astra is tempted. Astra knows they understand. That uncomfortable mutual knowledge is the cover.
PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The target display stays visually clean and attractive but behind the characters. It should not become the protagonist or cover more area than the human triangle.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; Astra's suspended decision and the two coworkers reading her; target display behind; maintenance calendar/work slates as context.
THUMBNAIL READ. Astra caught between two coworkers who are looking at her instead of the metric. The target is visible enough to explain pressure but not large enough to replace the people.
SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the cargo delay, benchmark values, Astra stopping the schedule, missed target, final report or the decision to reject output scheduling.

title: Issue 10 Cover — The Station Stays Open
summary: Character-first finale cover. Sell The Station Stays Open as the evolved ensemble answering together what Stardust is because each of them has spent the season being stubbornly, specifically themselves. The institutional fourth option is only the table they gather around. The real payoff is that these coworkers now function as a group without becoming interchangeable.
settingText: Main Bullpen / Admin Hub during the four-hour review: one worktable with the plain fourth-option sheet at its center, surrounded by real maintenance logs, lab records, route notes and privacy paperwork; the active station continues beyond them.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED ENSEMBLE CHARACTER COVER, deliberately echoing Issue 1's pleasure in the cast without repeating its posed lineup. Astra is central only because she is holding the pen over the plain fourth sheet. Around her, everybody is actively contributing in character: Mira slides in bounded lab evidence; Zib drops a blunt maintenance log/tool beside it; Jax adds route/operations notes; Glorp aligns the documentation; Kreeb deliberately leaves personal material out or protects a blank/private space.

RELATIONSHIP ENGINE. No one is gazing heroically at Astra and no one has become generic 'team member.' Their different habits are exactly what make the group useful. The image should feel like six coworkers interrupting, correcting and completing one another in a way that only works because they have history.

BOOKEND LOGIC. Issue 1 introduced a visually irresistible ensemble sharing a station. Issue 10 should show what that ensemble has become: not a family portrait, not a victory pose, but a working social organism. The visual rhyme is character density and warmth, not copied composition.

PROBLEM AS CATALYST. The blank fourth sheet is a shared working surface, not the hero object. Corporate option cards can sit off to one side as context; the cover's emotional center is the people leaning into the same problem from different directions.
FOCAL HIERARCHY. Masthead; active ensemble cluster and overlapping eye-lines/hands; Astra's pen/fourth sheet at the center of their interaction; institutional options last.

THUMBNAIL READ. A dense but readable semicircle of distinct silhouettes all converging on one shared table. It should immediately feel like 'the crew,' with enough individual posture difference that it never becomes a generic team shot.

SPOILER CEILING. Do not show the fourth option's final wording, Central approval, procurement improvement, permanent repair arrival, celebration or final status. The cover promises that these people will define the station together; it does not reveal whether the institution agrees.
